chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Sulayman, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the words of
God, Mighty and Majestic: 'And seek assistance with patience'

he said: 'Patience is fasting.' And he said: 'When an affliction and difficulty befalls a man, let him fast, for God, Mighty and Majestic, is saying: "And seek assistance with patience," meaning fasting.'

key_terms.الشَّدِيدَة: Severity/difficulty — a grave or intense trial
key_terms.الصَّبْر: Patience/endurance — interpreted here as fasting (sawm), revealing the esoteric dimension of the virtue
key_terms.الصِّيَام: Fasting — the Islamic practice of sawm, identified as the essence of sabr in this hadith
key_terms.النَّازِلَة: Calamity/affliction — a sudden hardship that descends upon a person
key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: Mighty and Majestic — a honorific for God emphasizing His power and glory

ai.seo_question: What does 'seek assistance with patience' mean in Quran 2:45 according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) provides an authoritative Shia exegesis of Quran 2:45, interpreting 'patience' (sabr) as a reference to 'fasting' (siyam). This interpretation links two pillars of Islamic practice: the virtue of patient endurance and the discipline of sawm. The teaching also provides a practical prescription — that when a believer faces hardship or calamity, fasting is the prescribed spiritual remedy, drawing on the strengthening power of the fast as the 'patience' God commands.
